premise.claim: The base status model cannot distinguish progress from blockers: RBG/RIS/RI controllers write no Progressing condition, RI has no persisted phase, and transient operation failures are recorded as lasting FailedScale/FailedUpdate facts (KEP-502 motivation).
premise.evidence: git grep on c2896cc0: RoleBasedGroupProgressing declared in api but never written by controllers; RoleInstanceSet/RoleInstance FailedScale/FailedUpdate written from 10 call sites; no RoleInstance status.phase field. See results/premise-and-suite.txt.

findings.title: Established RIS missing-instance classification flaps Recovering to ScalingUp after one reconcile
findings.claim: Under an established set with a still-missing required RoleInstance (recreation deferred), the RIS Progressing reason should be Recovering on every reconcile, but is ScalingUp from the second reconcile on.

tests.name: TestScaleUpAfterConvergenceStillReportsScalingUp
tests.note: control case guarding the fix: genuine target growth must stay ScalingUp

findings.proposedFix: establishedInstanceMissing should treat a persisted live Progressing reason of Recovering as durable prior-workflow evidence (mirroring the RBG layer's persisted-counter evidence), not only set.Status.Replicas >= target, which holds for exactly one reconcile.

findings.title: RBG does not propagate the RIS-level InvalidSpec blocker; reports a benign activity reason instead
findings.claim: A child RIS blocked by invalid committed ordinals reports Progressing=True(InvalidSpec); the RBG aggregation should surface a configuration-family blocker (needs attention), but reports RoleInstanceSetUpdated (activity).
findings.proposedFix: Map ProgressingReasonInvalidSpec in risReasonToRBG and include it in rbgCurrentBlocker's byFamily collection (configuration family already ranks first), or compute the equivalent fact at RBG preflight.

findings.title: Mixed-backend RBG keeps a stale controller-owned Progressing condition forever
findings.claim: When a role switches from RoleInstanceSet to a legacy backend, KEP-502 requires cleanup of controller-owned new-model output; updateRBGProgressingCondition returns nil and the stale Progressing condition is re-applied by the SSA patch indefinitely.
findings.proposedFix: In updateRBGProgressingCondition, RemoveStatusCondition(RoleBasedGroupProgressing) when !allRolesUseRoleInstanceSet, preserving external conditions.
findings.note: Round 2: unchanged code path; the stale controller-owned Progressing condition still rides the SSA status patch (patch payload captured in results/round2-contract-rbg.txt).

findings.title: RI layer keeps the first-appended blocker instead of competing through family precedence
findings.claim: When Scale and Update both fail in one reconcile, the finalized RI Progressing reason is the scale error regardless of family priority, dropping a higher-priority family (e.g. permission) that the RIS layer would have kept.
findings.proposedFix: Make instanceProgressingBlocker select by documented family priority (permission > admission > quota > resources > unclassified), as extractOwnSetBlocker does at the RIS layer.

findings.title: RIS/stateful read failures skip the status write instead of reporting Unknown(ObservationIncomplete)
findings.claim: ListRevisions / getInstanceSetRevisions failures in the stateful path return before ApplySetProgressingCondition and before any status write, so observedGeneration is not recorded on preflight failure; the RBG layer does write Unknown in the equivalent case.
findings.proposedFix: Report Progressing=Unknown(reason=ObservationIncomplete) with observedGeneration when the RIS preflight fails, mirroring updateRBGProgressingCondition's readErr branch.

findings.title: RI phase exits Creating/Updating one reconcile late
findings.claim: newStatus.Phase is computed from the pre-calculateStatus revision values (CurrentRevision not yet advanced), so the Running transition lands on the following reconcile. Cosmetic latency only.
findings.proposedFix: Compute the phase after calculateStatus advances CurrentRevision, or derive updateActive from the about-to-be-written revision equality.

findings.title: RBG confirmed blocker family lost on the roleErr path (round-1 ledger F3)
findings.claim: A confirmed current-generation blocker family survives the step-4 status recompute and an unclassifiable step-8 role error, and is cleared only by a fresh successful retry.
findings.proposedFix: Landed in effc2f8e as the entry-blocker snapshot (rbgEntryOwnBlocker) carried through aggregation and finalizeRBGProgressingCondition; test added this round to pin the new mechanism.

findings.title: Established set member loss during a readiness flap reports Creating instead of Recovering (revision regression)
findings.claim: An established set that converged, then flapped a pod's readiness (persisted Progressing=True/InstancesNotReady with ReadyReplicas<Replicas), then lost a member RoleInstance reports Recovering on every reconcile; on effc2f8e it reports Creating.

tests.name: TestEstablishedSetReadinessFlapThenMemberLossStaysRecovering
tests.note: PASS on previous head 95ddf06a, FAIL on effc2f8e (results/round2-differential-previous-head.txt); bites-checked with a discriminating fix (InstancesNotReady + completed-update-scope counters) that keeps the PR suite green

findings.proposedFix: Effc2f8e removed InstancesNotReady from setEstablishmentReasons to keep never-ready sets at Creating, but establishment evidence must distinguish never-ready from currently-unready durably (e.g. latch prior convergence, or count the condition as evidence only when the set previously completed its update scope: UpdatedReplicas >= ExpectedUpdatedReplicas with ExpectedUpdatedReplicas > 0 — note stateful synthetic slots inflate these counters, so a dedicated latch is safer).

findings.title: Own-operation blocker interlude destroys establishment evidence; post-blocker recovery reports Creating
findings.claim: An established set whose member-loss recovery was interrupted by a now-cleared own-operation blocker (persisted WaitingForQuota) reports Recovering while the replacement is pending; it reports Creating on both 95ddf06a and effc2f8e.

tests.name: TestEstablishedSetRecoveryAfterBlockerInterruptionStaysRecovering
tests.note: FAIL on both heads — pre-existing within this PR, not a round-2 regression

findings.proposedFix: Same root cause as F11: establishment evidence lives only in the persisted Progressing reason / counter shape and any intermediate write erases it. A durable establishment latch (or sticky workflow evidence like the RBG layer's persisted counters) fixes both.
